reason: This passage from Exodus 1-7 depicts God responding to the Israelites' suffering and oppression in Egypt with compassion and redemptive action. The text explicitly states that God heard their groaning (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם) and remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God's motivation is covenant faithfulness and compassion for the enslaved people, not anger at improper worship. The passage contains no mention of the people failing to worship or any worship-related transgressions. The subsequent plagues are directed at Pharaoh and Egypt to compel the release of the Israelites, not punishment of Israel for worship failures.
